LESSON: READING 11.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 11.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: where the actions are taking place using clues from pictures and the text, with peers. 1. How can we predict how a story, poem or conversation will end?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 11.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving – is enhanced as the learner relates the events in the text to everyday experiences.

• Creativity and imagination is enhanced as the learner makes predictions and anticipates possible outcomes in the story using pictures and

title.

Values:
Responsibility is enhanced as the learner takes up roles in retelling parts of the story in turns with peers

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (effective communication) is enhanced as the learner talks about where the actions in the story are taking place.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Comprehension of various texts is emphasized in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
